headline: The first acid trip in history ended with a bicycle ride home.
slides: Swiss chemist Albert Hofmann first made LSD at Sandoz in Basel on November 16, 1938. He was looking for a circulation and breathing stimulant.
Nobody saw a use for it. It sat untouched for five years.
Hofmann went back to it on a hunch. On April 16 he was accidentally exposed and felt something strange.
Three days later, on April 19, he took it deliberately to find out what it did.
It hit hard. Wartime rules kept cars off Basel's streets, so he and his assistant cycled home.
That ride is why April 19 is now known around the world as Bicycle Day.
sources: Sources: Albert Hofmann, LSD: My Problem Child; MAPS; Rolling Stone

the first acid trip ever was an accident, then an experiment, then a bike ride.
